subject: Cross-border eligibility & hosting options — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@eurobank.com>, EuroBank IT Procurement <procurement@eurobank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: Cross-border eligibility & hosting options — follow-up and next steps

Hi Sophie / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the time this morning — helpful call. I wanted to capture the high-level options we discussed and a short list of clarifying questions so we can scope next steps quickly.

Recap of hosting paths we covered:
- Hosted API (Redwood-hosted regional endpoints) — fastest to ship; requires that EU customer data at-rest is allowed in our EU region.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools in our EU region) — predictable throughput, customer isolation; supports customer-managed KMS for key separation.
- Private deployment (VPC / on-prem) — full control over network and storage residency; recommended for regulated workloads needing strict data locality.

Open questions from our side that will determine the recommended path:
1) For regulated accounts, does EuroBank require ALL data (including logs/telemetry) to remain within EU borders, or only primary customer data and PII?
2) Is compute outside the EU acceptable for anonymized/aggregated telemetry, or must processing also be EU-only?
3) Do you require customer-managed KMS/HSM integration for cryptographic separation?
4) What is the procurement timeline and any constraints around onboarding third-party SaaS in the EU?
5) Target performance SLOs (p95 latency) and expected qps for the first 3 months (helps us size Dedicated pools for a pilot).

Next steps I propose:
- Quick answers to the 5 questions above (email is fine).
- Security & residency questionnaire (I can send a short form) and SOC2 snapshot — I attached our one-page options overview to this note.
- Schedule a 30–45 minute call with your infra/security folks next week to review VPC options and KMS flow.

Attachments: redwood-residency-options.pdf (overview)

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
<signature stub>
From: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@eurobank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: EuroBank IT Procurement <procurement@eurobank.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Cross-border eligibility & hosting options — follow-up and next steps

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from EuroBank security/procurement:

- EU residency: For regulated customer data and anything that can identify a customer (PII), data must remain stored within EU member states. That includes logs if they contain identifiers. For telemetry that is fully anonymized and aggregated, we can accept cross-border processing, but we need a clear anonymization design first.
- Compute: Processing that involves PII must occur in the EU. Non-PII processing may be routable outside EU but only after we review the data flow.
- KMS/HSM: We require customer-managed keys for production stores containing PII. Integration with our Azure Key Vault (or HSM equivalent) is a must.
- Procurement: Procurement expects vendor security docs (SOC2), a master services annex for data residency clauses, and a standard vendor risk assessment; timeline is typically 6–8 weeks once we receive materials.
- Availability: For the pilot, we can accept low-single-digit minutes of planned downtime during deployment windows, but prefer canary-style rollouts that avoid customer impact.

If Redwood can provide a private VPC deployment plan for EU-only storage (and the option for Dedicated EU-only if we want managed hosting with customer KMS), we'd like to review costs and a technical onboarding checklist. Please include any notes on fallback behavior if an EU region becomes unavailable.

Regards,
Sophie Lambert
Head of Cloud Security — EuroBank

Attachment: eurobank-data-policy.pdf (internal reference)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-31T08:30:00Z
Subject: RE: Cross-border eligibility & hosting options — follow-up and next steps

Karthik / Marissa,

Good summary — based on Sophie's responses, here's what I recommend we package for EuroBank as options with clear tradeoffs: 

1) Private VPC (EU-only storage + compute):
   - Pros: Meets strict residency + KMS/HSM requirements, easier procurement sign-off for regulated workloads.
   - Cons: Higher. Onboarding involves network peering/VPN, SAML/OIDC setup, and an initial runbook for ops handover.

2) Dedicated capacity in Redwood EU region with customer-managed KMS:
   - Pros: Lower TCO than on-prem, faster to stand up than full VPC, supports customer KMS via BYOK integration.
   - Cons: Need contractual language to guarantee EU-only storage and clear fallback policy (avoid routing to APAC).

3) Hosted API EU regional endpoints (NOT recommended for PII-heavy workloads):
   - Pros: Fastest, lowest entry cost.
   - Cons: Only acceptable if EuroBank can certify anonymization for any data that leaves EU.

Action items for packaging a proposal:
- Send SOC2 one-pager and VPC onboarding checklist (attached in this thread).
- Draft language for the MSA/data residency annex that guarantees EU-at-rest and restricts cross-region routing for PII.
- Create a short tech appendix describing KMS integration options (Azure KV + HSM flow).
- Cost ballpark: Private VPC pilot (3 months) estimate: EUR 90k–140k depending on throughput and retention; Dedicated EU pool: EUR 30k–55k/month after pilot. (These are roughs; need QPS + retention to firm up).

I'll volunteer to own the procurement tracker with Sophie once they confirm names for the procurement and infra contacts. Proposed internal owner: Marissa for onboarding and PS scoping.

Ben
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: SOC2-brief.pdf, vpc-onboarding-checklist.docx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-06-01T15:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Cross-border eligibility & hosting options — follow-up and next steps

Sophie / Procurement team,

Appreciate the clarifications — that helps a lot. Based on your constraints, our recommended path to move quickly while keeping compliance and procurement momentum is:

Pilot proposal (recommended):
- Scope: Private VPC deployment limited to EU region for all PII and customer data (no cross-border storage).
- Duration: 3 months pilot with defined ramp (we'll provide throughput sizing guidance once you confirm expected qps/peak).
- Security: Customer-managed KMS integration (Azure Key Vault) and SOC2 snapshot provided.
- Rollouts: Canary updates and no forced global failover that routes PII outside EU; fallback models will be explicit in the MSA.

Immediate next steps (we can start these in parallel):
1) EuroBank to confirm the procurement and infra contacts we should engage with (name + email).
2) EuroBank to complete the short security/residency questionnaire — I attached the one-page form.
3) Exchange network ranges and preferred connectivity model (VPN vs ExpressRoute/Direct Connect).
4) I will provision a draft MSA annex and a technical appendix addressing KMS flow and fallback rules for your review.

I attached the options overview, SOC2 brief, and the VPC onboarding checklist for your team. If that looks good, can we schedule a 45-minute technical review on Wednesday or Thursday next week? Here are two time slots that work for us: Wednesday 2027-06-08 10:00–10:45 CET or Thursday 2027-06-09 14:00–14:45 CET.

Thanks again — we'll keep the proposal pragmatic and aligned to procurement timelines.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
